headline: GOLD ERASES ALL 2026 GAINS: JOBS SHOCK CRUSHES FED CUT BETS, METAL POSTS WORST WEEK OF YEAR
snippet: Gold plunged 3.27% to $4,340/oz on Friday after May nonfarm payrolls printed at 172,000 — nearly double the 85,000 forecast — erasing all of gold's 2026 year-to-date gains in a single session. Silver fell nearly 3% in its sharpest single-session drop since April 2025, with the broad precious metals selloff driven by a surging U.S. dollar and rapidly unwinding Fed rate-cut expectations.

headline: GOLDSEEK COT JUNE 5: LARGE SPECS CUT GOLD LONGS SHARPLY AFTER JOBS SHOCK — NEW DRIVERS MAY OVERRIDE HISTORY
snippet: The June 5 Commitment of Traders report shows large speculators aggressively cutting gold long positions in the wake of the May jobs shock, with historical COT patterns pointing to potential further near-term downside. GoldSeek's analyst cautions that the Iran conflict's geopolitical premium may override normal COT signals, creating an unusual split between momentum-driven paper positioning and structural physical demand.

headline: CHINA IMPORTED 790+ TONS OF SILVER IN EARLY 2026 — SOLAR BOOM KEEPS PHYSICAL MARKET STRUCTURALLY TIGHT
snippet: Despite Friday's paper-market selloff, China's physical silver demand remains structurally intact: 790+ tonnes of silver imports in early 2026 reflect booming solar panel production with no near-term substitute. The Gold SWOT analysis notes the Silver Institute projects 227 million ounces of physical investment in 2026 — the highest since 2022 — providing a fundamental demand floor that diverges sharply from short-term futures positioning.

headline: DPM METALS HITS 713 METRES AT 2.52 G/T AuEq IN MAJOR PORPHYRY DISCOVERY ADJACENT TO CHELOPECH MINE
snippet: DPM Metals (TSX: DPM) announced a major gold-copper porphyry discovery at Brevene South in Bulgaria — just 1km from the operating Chelopech mine boundary — sending shares up 3% on Wednesday. The standout hole cut 713m at 1.31 g/t Au and 1.16% Cu from 1,172m depth, including a higher-grade core of 398m at 1.48 g/t Au and 1.45% Cu still in progress. Seven drill rigs are deployed across the licence area, with 15,000m of additional drilling planned for 2026.

headline: AYA GOLD & SILVER HITS BONANZA 2,176 G/T SILVER OVER 8.4M UNDERGROUND AT ZGOUNDER, MOROCCO
snippet: Aya Gold & Silver (TSX: AYA) released bonanza-grade drill results from its Zgounder Mine in Morocco, headlined by 2,176 g/t Ag over 8.4m underground — including a peak of 4,298 g/t over 3.6m — alongside open-pit intercepts of 1,867 g/t Ag over 6m and 1,160 g/t Ag over 6m in separate holes. CEO Benoit La Salle said the results confirm strong continuity of silver mineralization in both the pit and central underground zone.

headline: JUNIOR MINER REPORTS MULTI-MILLION-OZ GOLD-SILVER BREAKTHROUGH IN ARGENTINA'S SALTA PROVINCE
snippet: A TSX-listed junior explorer expanded its gold-silver-copper porphyry project in Salta, Argentina — one of the continent's most mining-friendly jurisdictions — adding new concession area and advancing its 2026 drill program. The company is targeting a potentially multi-million-ounce system, with initial assay results expected within 60 days as majors increasingly scout the region for acquisition targets at elevated gold prices.

headline: Q2 METALS FILES 295 MT LITHIUM RESOURCE AT CISCO, QUEBEC — AMONG CANADA'S LARGEST SPODUMENE DEPOSITS
snippet: Q2 Metals (TSX-V: QTWO) filed its inaugural NI 43-101 resource estimate for the Cisco lithium project in Quebec's James Bay region — an inferred 295 Mt at 1.36% Li2O, placing it among Canada's largest spodumene deposits. Winter 2026 drilling delivered 264.6m at 1.84% Li2O in a single hole. A summer drill program commences mid-June as energy storage lithium demand is forecast to grow 55% year-over-year in 2026.

headline: RARE EARTH SIGNALS CHANGING: DYSPROSIUM AND TERBIUM ACCESS NOW SCARCER THAN PRICE — JUNE 1-5 WEEKLY
snippet: The week of June 1-5 saw a critical inflection in rare earth dynamics: for heavy rare earths dysprosium and terbium — essential for permanent magnets with no Western substitute — physical access has become more constrained than price alone indicates. China's export licensing approval rates for European buyers have fallen below 25% in some categories since April 2025 controls began, with price spikes of up to sixfold reported for approved lots.

headline: GOLD MINERS GENERATING TECH-LIKE 40% NET MARGINS — YET JUNIOR TSXV STOCKS STILL TRADE AT FRACTIONS OF NAV
snippet: With gold trading near $4,400 and industry-wide all-in sustaining costs below $2,000/oz, senior gold producers are posting net margins that rival Silicon Valley — Newmont reported $7.3 billion in free cash flow last year. Yet TSX-V gold juniors continue to trade at steep discounts to net asset value, a disconnect analysts attribute to still-early institutional allocation and sector stigma from past newsletter pump cycles that has yet to fully unwind.

headline: JUNIOR GOLD MINERS RISING FAST BUT STILL AT FRACTIONS OF NAV — ANALYSTS SAY THE BIGGEST MOVE IS STILL AHEAD
snippet: Despite doubling and tripling from 2025 lows, most TSX-V gold explorers remain priced at fractions of their net asset values — even as gold approaches $5,000 and seniors post record free cash flow. Analysts point to operating leverage at extreme levels, accelerating M&A interest from cash-rich majors hunting reserve replacements, and still-early institutional participation as the combination that could rapidly close the valuation gap for quality junior names.
